input_findings_summary: 8 findings from the in-context proposal pass (iteration 2): 0 CRITICAL, 4 WARNING, 4 SUGGESTION.
pushback_verification: All 8 verified against current state before any edit; zero stale. Independently re-checked rather than taken from the report: the delta contains no occurrence of `--sources` or `orbit validate` as a surface statement (finding 1 holds); `schemas/spec-driven/schema.yaml:2` carries `version: 4` as a YAML number, so the string claim is load-bearing (finding 3); design D3's four table rows agree with the spec's, so finding 5 is a duplication risk and not a live disagreement; the stranded lead-in is at the end of the within-file paragraph exactly as reported (finding 8). Entries below are generated FROM the review emit's findings array, so titles and files are byte-identical to the pass they resolve — the fix adopted after the previous walk's corrective re-emit.

resolutions.title: No requirement names the surface the lint is reached through
resolutions.action: Added a surface paragraph to requirement 1: the lint is reached through `orbit validate --sources`, `--all` runs it alongside the change and spec checks, a finding fails validation with a non-zero exit, coverage renders after the findings on both, and per-item `orbit validate <change>`/`<spec>` are UNCHANGED — with the reason stated (a project-scoped verdict under a per-change name is the wrong frame). The delta can now be read end to end and learn what invokes it.

resolutions.title: Task 1.3 is short of the malformed-registry scenario it has to satisfy
resolutions.action: Rewrote task 1.3 to name EVERY fault the malformed-registry scenario lists — unparseable YAML, a non-map `sources:`, a scalar entry, a duplicate source name, a missing `engine:`, an unknown `engine:` value, a missing required parameter, an unknown key — and to carry the scenario's own framing that an existing file SHALL NOT be able to reach the absent-file silence. Task 5.1's 'each error path' now inherits the full list.

resolutions.title: The spec never states that a source emits a STRING, and one of the four is a YAML number
resolutions.action: Added a sentence above the source table: every engine source emits a STRING, and a natively numeric fact (`version: 4` is a YAML number) is rendered to decimal string form AT THE SOURCE, never at the comparison — the check performs no coercion of its own. The spec now carries what design D2 and task 1.2 already assumed.

resolutions.title: The pairing table mixes parse errors with a check failure, and says nothing about blast radius
resolutions.action: Split the pairing table into KIND and OUTCOME columns and stated the two kinds explicitly: a MARKER ERROR names the offending delimiter (no span exists to compare), a CHECK FAILURE names the source value against the span's text. The empty-span row is now typed CHECK FAILURE so it can never be emitted as a syntax error. Blast radius settled under R-crc-3 and stated: a marker error abandons ONE FILE's remaining spans and reports, while every other file still lints — the run fails but never goes quiet, so one malformed marker cannot turn the lint into a project-wide no-op. Task 2.2 carries both.

resolutions.title: The v1 source table now exists in two places, which is the defect this change argues against
resolutions.action: Marked the spec's requirement-1 table NORMATIVE and design D3's the annotated copy, with the tie-break stated: if keeping the two in step ever costs anything, the spec's survives — citing this change's own proposal, which rejects a capability split on the ground that two copies of one rule is a defect.

resolutions.title: `prefix` matching and `<n>` are unspecified
resolutions.action: Stated the grammar: `<prefix>` is matched LITERALLY, never compiled as a pattern, and `<n>` is one or more decimal digits with nothing following — so `R-crc-10` is an entry and `R-crc-4a` is not.

resolutions.title: `specs.capability-count` does not say what it counts over
resolutions.action: Replaced 'the count of baseline capability specs' with the countable shape: directories under the project's `specs/` that contain a `spec.md`, BASELINE only (a capability introduced by an unarchived change is not counted), and a directory without a `spec.md` is not counted.

resolutions.title: The exclusion-table lead-in got stranded behind the within-file digression
resolutions.action: Moved the exclusion lead-in back to the end of the living-versus-records paragraph where it belongs, and gave the table its own short introducer, so it no longer reads as though the author's marker were one of the path exclusions.

final_assessment: All 8 findings resolved in the obvious-fix lane; no decision fork, nothing deferred, nothing escalated, no ripple outside the change. One method call was settled under R-crc-3 and named for reversal: a marker error's blast radius is ONE FILE, not the run. The change still stands at 18 tasks and 1 capability — every resolution was a sentence, a table column, or a task amendment, and the spec gained the one thing it was missing, a statement of what invokes it.
